name: modern-web-guidance-src
description: Keep your coding agent up to date with the latest web best practices
one_liner: The behind-the-scenes repo where Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Mozilla write and test the 'cheat sheet' that teaches AI coding assistants modern web coding practices — this repo itself is the authoring/testing tooling, not the cheat sheet you'd install.
buyer: Honestly: nobody. This is internal tooling for browser-vendor standards teams, not a product anyone outside that group would pay for.
business_use_cases: A browser vendor's web-platform team uses it to author and score the guidance content before publishing it.
A contributor to web standards proposes a new best-practice rule and uses the eval dashboard to check it doesn't regress agent behavior.
None of this reaches an outside buyer — the actual installable product is the separate GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance repo, which is itself free.

money_ideas.idea: There isn't a real one here — it's a free, vendor-backed standards project with no commercial surface

steal_this: Nothing to build directly from this repo. If you want to monetize the idea behind it, go build a paid 'keep my coding agent current' subscription service on top of the public guidance it produces instead.
